#### Description
The `NullBuyingPowerModel` considers that we have sufficient buying power for all orders.

Adds an example using a bull call spread since an equity buy and hold would not show the impact of this model in the position group buying power model.

#### Related Issue
Closes #3157

#### Motivation and Context
The buying power model prevents orders in live trading if it considers there is not sufficient buying power. If users want to submit the orders, they can use this model to bypass the validation. 

#### Requires Documentation Change
Yes. List this model on
https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/buying-power

#### How Has This Been Tested?
Regression tests.

issue_context.title: Implement NullMarginModel for Live Trading
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Live trading should lean on the brokerage margin limitations and not impose them in LEAN.

#### Actual Behavior
LEAN models restrict brokerage margin.

#### Potential Solution
1) Improve option margin models
2) and Implement null margin model to disable restrictions for live trading.

#### Reproducing the Problem
Live trading straddles.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
comments: Are there any updates on this request? Implementing a NullMarginModel will open up a much wider array of options strategies that can be deployed via QuantConnect. Thank you!
This would be very valuable to me as well.
Has this issue been resolved? Is there a way to turn off margin limitations for options?

- Confirm if same or different to ConstantBuyingPowerModel
 - If same; then add a shim NullMarginModel with default 0.001 (tiny incase account currency BTC)
 - Add an example algorithm using it.
 - https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Common/Securities/ConstantBuyingPowerModel.cs

review_comments: Would of expected it to use the https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Common/Securities/ConstantBuyingPowerModel.cs with a small value because it's not only about placing a new trading but the margin used to maintain it without getting a margin call?

Users could use the `MarginCallModel.Null` to handle the margin calls. Regardless, I  added the `NullBuyingPowerModel.GetMaintenanceMargin` returning a `MaintenanceMargin` of zero. It means the total margin used is always zero and margin calls will not be triggered.

This feature is inspired by the  `ConstantBuyingPowerModel`. I didn't inherit from that class, because `ConstantBuyingPowerModel.GetInitialMarginRequirement` gives us a very small initial margin that leads to a very large quantity if we use `SetHoldings` or `CalculateOrderQuantity`. If the algorithm is using `SetHoldings` the author would have to rewrite it.
